To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the definitions of parton densities and soft factors in the factorization formula for the Drell-Yans process can be chosen to be universal, i.e., the same as for the other hard-scattering processes.

(i) the soft factor in factorization for the Drell-Yans process is the same as the one for semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering, (ii) the soft factor for e(+)e(+) annihilation is different, (iii) there is a time reversal transformation of parton densities and soft factors that relates the soft factors for Drell-Yan scattering and semi-inclusive deep scattering and (iv) the soft factors for the three processes are all the same in the limit

the definitions of the parton densities, the fragmentation functions, and the soft factor are universal in e(+)e (-) annihilation, Drell-Yan, and semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering, and that the only modification of the factorization formulae needed to remove rapidities divergences is to replace lightlike Wilson lines by a choice of directions consistent with factorization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factorization of hard-scattering processes in Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD).
the universality of soft and/or collinear factors in QCD factorizations.
the factorization of hard-scattering cross sections into universal parton densities and fragmentation functions and process-dependent soft functions, which can be calculated in perturbation theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factorization of hard-scattering cross sections is independent of the directions of the Wilson lines, provided that they are lightlike and the rapidity divergencies are removed.
the soft and collinear factorization formula for the cross section of the Drell-Yann process is universal and process independent, as it should be.
the universality of the soft and collinear parts in QCD hard-scattering factorizations is restored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the factorization theorems for e(+)e- annihilation, DIS, and Drell-Yan are identical, with only the soft function differing by a time-reversed transformation.
the definitions of the collinear factors are universal and that the definitions of soft factors are process dependent, but that the soft factors are always related to each other by time reversal.

the definitions of the collinear and soft functions are unique, and that their universality is unique except for a time-reversibility transformation between the Drell-Yann process and e(+)e annihilation and SIDIS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the universality of soft factors is not spoiled by the process dependence, but that the universality is modified by the time-reversal properties of the soft factor and parton densities.
the Wilson-line directions are not arbitrary and should be chosen with care.
factorization is not process dependent, as long as we choose the Wilson lines consistently.
